newsitem.title: CANADA: CAW rejects Canadian Air wage-cut plan.
newsitem.headline: CAW rejects Canadian Air wage-cut plan.

text.p: The Canadian Auto Workers said on Friday its Canadian Airlines bargaining committee unanimously rejected the ailing carrier's survival plan and its call for 10 percent rollbacks in employee wages.
The CAW, which represents 3,700 passenger and reservation agents, joins the International Association of Machinists in rejecting Canadian's wage cuts on Friday.

Canadian said the plan -- which includes adding U.S. and Asian capacity and cutting domestic routes -- was necessary to avert a cash crunch in the first quarter of 1997 and to return the airline to profitability in four years.
The plan also asks AMR Corp, which owns 33 percent of the airline, to make concessions to the fees that Canadian pays each year for various computer and management services.
"At every financial crisis the workers have given but the company keeps coming back for more -- under the false notion that this will save the company," said CAW president Buzz Hargrove.
"The concession demands are more about appearances for the banks. In reality they will simply further rachet down airline wages."
The CAW said meetings were scheduled with its membership across Canada beginning November 7 in Toronto.

Union officials with the 5,300-member IAM said on Friday that they would not take Canadian's proposals back to members and that a collective agreement approved earlier this year would stand. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
